output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is almost certainly due to the Finance credit-limit change on 14 April, not the new starters. That change cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger cases to the back-office billing team. Billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in one week. Referred calls resolve at about 33% and non-referred at 82%, and neither rate changed. Referral rates are the same across tenure bands, and tenured agents fell by the same amount (75% to 67%). So the new starters, the tariff rise and the IVR are not the main drivers. Tariff enquiries resolve at 85% and are unchanged. Customer Operations wasn't consulted on the change. Don't put April-intake agents on performance plans; the data doesn't support blaming them. Next step: agree a revised credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling, and trial it on two teams for six weeks. Track first-contact resolution and the unsupported-credit rate. Finance has said it would accept this kind of trial. I'm fairly confident about the cause. The IVR and workload effects were not tested directly, so the confidence is lower there. Complaints rose, but the evidence doesn't show they came from the FCR fall.
